review_notes: I read the whole file and the definition of multinomialMeasure, which has no DecidableEq. I searched the repository for uses of categoricalMeasure and found none outside this file. The other simp lemmas look fine. categoricalMeasure_def is correctly not simp. map_categoricalMeasure has a Fintype target, so it can't overlap with the one-hot lemma, whose target is `I → ℕ`. My one finding is the classical local instance in the statement of the simp lemma. I could not run Lean, so I don't know whether the generic-instance version will compile. I expect the proof to work with `classical` removed or kept.

findings.excerpt: local instance categoricalDecidableEq : DecidableEq I := Classical.decEq I
findings.problem: The `@[simp]` lemma's LHS contains `Pi.single i 1`, and its `DecidableEq I` instance is the section-local `Classical.decEq I`. That instance is baked into the exported statement. A user's `(categoricalMeasure p).map (fun i ↦ Pi.single i 1)` on `Fin n` or any type with its own `DecidableEq` instance elaborates `Pi.single` with that instance, e.g. `instDecidableEqFin`. These instances are not reducibly defeq to `Classical.decEq`. So simp will most likely fail to match the rule for any concrete or generic `[DecidableEq I]` category type. That defeats the purpose of marking it simp and the stated link to the multinomial API.
findings.proposed_change: Remove the local classical instance and state the lemma with a `[DecidableEq I]` argument, so the simp rule matches whichever instance the user has. `multinomialMeasure` does not depend on `DecidableEq`, so the RHS is unaffected. Keep the proof's `classical` only where needed, or drop it. If the generic statement doesn't compile, state the simp lemma for arbitrary `[DecidableEq I]` and keep a classical corollary separately.
findings.benefit: The simp rule `map (Pi.single · 1) (categoricalMeasure p) = multinomialMeasure 1 p` would fire on the user's own one-hot encodings, not only on terms built with `Classical.decEq`. It would also drop a hidden classical instance from the public statement.
